content.title: DRAGONS DOWN: WILDLANDS
content.content:
![](/images/pdf/37f74aa0bbf43addc356a799f1c65d453770f235.jpeg)

![](/images/pdf/cb8d1a78f16dacefdd2092d9fa0cbe141ceb3400.jpeg)

Version 1.4. September 28, 2026

*“Pushing deeper into the wilderness, we found places few had dared to* *explore even before the dragons came. Dense thickets stretched beneath* *canopies of Green interspersed with wild hills. Hidden dangers were in* *every shadowed hollow. Yet there were rumors of forgotten places and* *strange peoples within. I decided to venture into these wildlands to* *discover what adventures await....”*

**Dragons Down: Wildlands** expands Dragons Down by introducing weather and two new Terrain Packs. New components for the Wildlands expansion are marked with a small ![inline](/images/pdf/b81beb4450eca6cfb341eeeb750e2790852f033e.jpeg) in one corner. Counters, round cardboard tokens, and Hero Chips do not have a mark.

content.title: Game Setup
content.content:
Players may choose from any of the Terrain Packs, including the two new packs introduced in the Wildlands expansion, in any combination. Shuffle the Map Tiles from the chosen Terrain Packs together to create the Map Tile stack as normal. Players may also select any Lineage and Class for any game of Dragons Down.

The Tangled Thickets Terrain Pack is a dangerous place, featuring four Treasure Sites filled with exotic treasures and protected by the dangers of the jungle.

The Hostile Hills Terrain Pack is a perilous land featuring three Treasure Sites, along with Monsters and Natives unique to its rugged terrain.

content.title: Thickets Clearings
content.content:
![float-right](/images/pdf/468d62a7bdd0ef57b64270add4bc0d1368722b8a.jpeg) Tangled Thickets Map Tiles include Thickets Clearings, marked with a purple Thickets icon. Entering a Thickets Clearing costs 2 actions, even if the Hero is using flying movement. A flying Hero pays no additional movement cost when entering a Thickets Clearing from an adjacent Map Tile.

Thickets Clearings are overgrown with dense foliage, providing ample opportunities to hide. When using the optional Terrain Effects rules, treat Thickets Clearings as Woods Clearings. Thickets Clearings have no other effect on combat.

The Tangled Thickets include some unique monsters with special rules as spelled out in the Monster Manifest in the Appendix of these rules.

content.title: Hills Clearings
content.content:
![float-right](/images/pdf/f0fc8d10e8c142589ac17f410ca7965a7e8a1980.jpeg) Hostile Hills tiles introduce a new type of clearing called a Hills Clearing, marked with a brown Hills icon. Hills Clearings represent areas elevated above the surrounding lands.

Entering a Hills Clearing costs 2 actions unless the Hero is entering from another Hills Clearing or a Mountain Clearing. A Hero using flying movement pays only 1 action to enter a Hills Clearing.

The Hostile Hills include some unique monsters with special rules as spelled out in the Monster Manifest in the Appendix of these rules.

content.title: OPTIONAL RULES
content.content: Optional rules allow players to customize their experience with Dragons Down. Most of these rules slightly increase the complexity of the game and may be mixed and matched in a modular fashion to maximize thematic immersion and enjoyment.

content.title: Weather
content.content:
Weather in Dragons Down introduces changing conditions that affect Heroes as they explore the realm. Each Weather Card represents a specific type of weather or effect, how long it remains in effect, and the effects it has on the game. Some Weather Cards are limited to certain seasons.

Weather can be used with any game modes or scenarios.

content.title: Weather Cards
content.content:
Weather Cards contain information on how it is applied in the game.

**Weather Type:** The name at the top of the card identifies the type of weather the card represents.

**Duration:** The numbered spaces show how many turns the weather lasts (*this is also shown* *in the lower left of the card*).

**Weather Reveal:** One of the Duration boxes on the Weather Card indicates when the next Weather Card is revealed.

**Game Effects:** These symbols show the rules that are in effect while this Weather Card is active. *For example, the Cold Weather Card shown above indicates that a Hero* *that spends any portion of their turn unsheltered (outside of a Civilization Location or* *Cave Clearing) must either spend an action or take a wound of their choice.*

**Seasons:** The symbols along the bottom of the card indicate the seasons in which this type of weather can occur. The available Seasons are, in order on the cards, Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter.

![Annotated weather card reference](/images/annotations/c2a766c5ef182c7d59f8facb937d2410a1c61591.png)

content.title: Game Setup
content.content:
To include weather in a game, players first choose a Season, either by choice or randomly. Only one Season is used for the entire game.

Remove all Weather Cards that do not show the chosen Season symbol at the bottom of the card. Shuffle the remaining cards and deal 8 of them face down to form the Weather Pile. Return all unused Weather Cards to the box without revealing them.

Reveal the top card of the Weather Pile and place it near the game board. Place a pink Status Cube on the first Duration box. This Weather Card is now active and its Game Effects apply.

Reveal the top card of the Weather Pile and place it near the game board. Place a pink Status Cube on the first Duration box. This Weather Card is now active and its Game Effects apply.

content.title: Weather Progression
content.content:
At the end of the Battle Phase of each turn, check the active Weather Card.

If there is another Duration box, advance the pink Status Cube to that box. If the cube enters a box containing a Weather Reveal symbol, reveal the top card of the Weather Pile and place it next to the active Weather Card. This is the next Weather Card that will enter play, but it is not yet active. It is revealed to give players a glimpse of the weather to come for planning purposes.

It is important to ensure that all players understand the Game Effects of upcoming Weather Cards.

If there is no next Duration box, the active weather ends. If a next Weather Card has been revealed, it becomes the new active Weather Card. Place it on top of the previous Weather Card, leaving the number in the lower-left corner of the previous card visible as a turn counter. Place the pink Status Cube on the first Duration box of the new active Weather Card. Its Game Effects apply to the next turn of the game.

If there is no next Weather Card when the active weather ends, the game ends. Process game end normally for the mode or scenario you are playing.

Effects due to Weather Cards are in addition to any other terrain effects (*e.g.* *movement costs, wounds from Desert Clearings, etc.*)

Each Weather Card is explained in detail in the Weather Card Manifest on page 4.

content.title: Sheltered and Unsheltered Clearings
content.content:
Weather Cards introduce the concept of Sheltered and Unsheltered Clearings.

A Clearing is Sheltered if it is a Cave or if it contains a Civilization Location.

A Clearing is unsheltered if it does not contain a Civilization Location and is not a Cave Clearing.

content.title: Enhanced Alert
content.content: When performing an Alert Action, in addition to rearranging equipment, the Hero chooses one of the following benefits. A Hero may perform multiple Alert Actions during a single turn. A Hero must choose a different alert type for each Alert Action.

content.title: Normal Alert
content.content: During combat this turn, the Hero may place +1 Speed Cube in each round of combat. Place a pink Status Cube on the Alert Box on the Hero Board to indicate that the Hero has chosen Normal Alert this turn.

contentNodes.markdown: During combat this turn, the Hero may place +1 Speed Cube in each round of combat. Place a pink Status Cube on the Alert Box on the Hero Board to indicate that the Hero has chosen Normal Alert this turn.

content.title: Magic Alert
content.content:
Choose 1 healthy Magic Cube and place it in the Alert Box on the Hero Board. If the alerted Magic Cube is used to cast a Spell during combat this turn, that Spell gains +1 Attack Speed, even if all Attack Speed boxes are filled. At the end of the round in which the Spell is cast, move the alerted Magic Cube to the Wounded Box.

An alerted Magic Cube may not be placed in a Spell Box showing a wound symbol. If the alerted Magic Cube is not used to cast a Spell during combat that turn, return it to the Healthy Box.

content.title: Missile Alert
content.content: Place a pink Status Cube on the Ranged Attack icon of an equipped Ranged Weapon Card (*not a Spell Card*). A Hero may only have one Ranged Weapon Card alerted at a time. During combat this turn, when attacking with that weapon, if both Ranged Attack Dice results are negative, the Hero may reroll both dice. If only one, or none, of the Ranged Attack Dice results are negative, then they may not be rerolled.

content.title: Specialists
content.content:
![float-right](/images/pdf/0ac157d86509aa3f5b32be5dad738fd0d9f305c8.jpeg) Throughout the realm, Heroes may encounter remarkable Specialists whose rare talents provide assistance unavailable anywhere else. When using this optional rule, shuffle the Specialist Tokens and place them in a convenient location. Whenever an empty Civilization Token is drawn at a Civilization Location, replace it with a random Specialist Token.

Each Specialist offers a unique service or ability that Heroes may use when they encounter them. Specialists are not Merchants and provide none of the services that Heroes may normally perform. Specialists only offer their unique services, which may be purchased by performing a Trade Action with that Specialist.

The Base Price for each Specialist’s service is shown below and on their token. The Starting Price is 3 times the Base Price. Heroes may haggle following the standard Haggle rules using their lowest attribute.

All Specialists are explained in the Specialists Manifest on page 4.

content.title: Stubborn Guardians
content.content: Guardians return to the Monster Trays only when the Monsters Return arrow without the dot is rolled (*on the Summoning Die from the Core* ***Dragons Down*** *Game*). All other Monsters return when either Monsters Return arrow is rolled.

content.title: Banished Heroes
content.content:
Your hero starts the game banished.

**Ruthless Riverlands Not in Play:** Shuffle all Map Tiles together and place a random wilderness Map Tile to start. The Hero is placed in a random Clearing at game start.

**Ruthless Riverlands in Play:** Players start their Hero in a random Ruthless Riverlands wilderness Map Tile. Place the Hero Chip in a random Dock Clearing.

After placing the Hero Chip, reveal and place a Wilderness Token before taking any actions.

For added difficulty, combine this optional rule with the Wits Only optional rule from the Core **Dragons Down** Game

![](/images/pdf/06df3e174b31d1437b8ddc537afd4994a0048d3a.jpeg)

content.title: Corrupted
content.content:
Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. At the beginning of each turn, randomly select one magic color. Until the end of the turn, magic cubes of the selected color may not be used for any purpose, and no enchantments of that color may occur. Immediately remove all existing enchantments of the selected color.

These restrictions also apply to Monsters and Natives, but do not affect a Dragon’s Fireball.

content.title: Diviner (Shard Charge)
content.content: Diviner can channel magical energy into a shard they always have with them, enhancing its power. Using an alert action may place a healthy magic cube on the shard space of their class card (*returning any cube already there* *to their healthy box*). During combat, this cube counts as two cubes of the same color when casting spells. If the cube is wounded during combat, the effect is immediately canceled. At the end of combat the cube is returned to the Hero’s healthy box.

content.title: Gravesworn (Dead Speech)
content.content:
The Gravesworn is protector and researcher of all things undead. Undead do not block or target the Gravesworn, nor may the Gravesworn, or their hired natives, target the undead (*including attacks that target* *the entire Clearing like Fiery Chasm or Earthquake*). The Gravesworn may not loot treasure sites whose protectors are undead Guardians. The Gravesworn may have one undead Monster as a minion (*hired native*) at any time as follows.

Using a normal Hire Action, the Gravesworn must haggle to reduce the hire price to 1x. The Gravesworn only fails in a haggle attempt by rolling a door symbol. The Gravesworn pays no actual cost to hire an undead Monster. All other Hired Natives rules apply (*From* **Dragons Down: Natives & Legends**). Monsters belong to no group. Thus, a closed door result on a haggle attempt does not prevent the Gravesworn from hiring other undead Monsters on that same turn, even the same Monster type. The Gravesworn loses Fame when their minion is killed.

The Gravesworn may not attempt to hire a Monster while they already have a minion. The Gravesworn may not fly using a hired minion (*unlike the Beastmaster*).

content.title: Shaman (Totemic Projection)
content.content:
The Shaman casts their spirit beyond the bounds of their body, sensing what lies unseen. Shamans may perform a search action in an adjacent map tile containing no wilderness or civilization tokens. Upon a successful search, place a matching token(s) face-down in the tile. The hero may look it, but may not reveal it. No special tokens are triggered.

If playing using the exploration rules, the hero may explore as if in a mountain clearing to place a map tile, but must search in order to place tokens per the rules explained above.

content.title: The Cult
content.content:
No one really knows who leads the cult and their members are hard to distinguish. At the end of any combat round in which the Cult Leader is killed, replace the dead Cult Leader chip with a Cult Member chip.

- If any Cult Members are still alive in the combat, randomly choose one and replace its chip with the Cult Leader chip with the same side facing up. Place the replaced Cult Member chip in the Hero’s Trophy Pile.

- If no Cult Members remain in the combat, replace the dead Cult Leader chip with a Cult Member chip from the Monster Tray.

- If there are no Cult Members remaining in either the combat or the Monster Tray, congratulations, you killed the actual Cult Leader. Place the Cult Leader chip in the Hero’s Trophy Pile.

content.title: Revenant
content.content:
The Revenant casts Foresight while on the front side of its chip. Each time the Revenant casts Foresight, set one of the Summoning Dice as follows, in order:

- **First Foresight:** Set the Local Monster Symbol Die to the symbol matching the Map Tile where the Revenant is located.

- **Second Foresight:** Set the Wandering Monster Symbol Die to the symbol matching the Map Tile where the Revenant is located.

- **Third Foresight:** Set the Local Monster Number Die to its highest-numbered side.

- **Fourth Foresight:** Set the Wandering Monster Number Die to its highest-numbered side.

- **Fifth Foresight:** The spell has no effect.

contentNodes.markdown: Base Price: 2 Gold. Starting Price: 6 Gold. Move to a Clearing of your choice containing a revealed Gate without spending a Move Action.

content.title: Healer
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/bc8f0a400a48d5a9e02f0ac10536e9d275e0dc60.jpeg) Base Price: 1 Gold per cube. Starting Price: 3 Gold per cube. Choose how many cubes to heal before rolling any Haggle Dice. Haggle to determine the price per cube, then multiply that price by the number of cubes healed.

content.title: Magus
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/afaedb32ffc83973151deed55cf7e26d965246f7.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold + the Spell’s Price. Starting Price: 3 times the Base Price. Learn 1 Spell Card attached to an equipped Treasure Card. Does not require rolling the Learn Dice.

content.title: Pathfinder
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/427f2e9c24a7d7ea2238523ed78ccbdfde333674.jpeg) Base Price: 2 Gold. Starting Price: 6 Gold. Find 1 face-up Hidden Path of your choice on a Map Tile up to 2 Map Tiles away from the Pathfinder.

contentNodes.markdown: Base Price: 2 Gold. Starting Price: 6 Gold. Find 1 face-up Hidden Path of your choice on a Map Tile up to 2 Map Tiles away from the Pathfinder.

content.title: Telecrafter
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/a8ff0561b27b941956878f0637414ed618cc5faa.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold. Starting Price: 9 Gold. Teleport to a random Clearing on a Map Tile of your choice up to 2 Map Tiles away.
